title: Elegy for the Don
subtitle: The tattered banner still billows in the wind as the first snow falls.

items.text: Elegy for the Don
The red willow that has watched over the Cossacks for over a century lies fractured.
The ground that should have been firm and warm has turned to a sticky mire, trapping Igor by the legs.
Blood courses through his already throbbing veins as the power borrowed from Baba Yaga puts an almost unbearable burden on his mixed-blood arcanist body.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: You've grown stronger.
Pinned like a hunted beast, he can only watch as the enemy commander approaches.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Hm. Admiral Igor.
Krutov stops a few paces away.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Still catching your breath from the teleport ritual?
Igor only glares, his chest heaving. Krutov knows this proud old lion will not plead, not even in his last moments.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Don't worry. I'll soon put you out of your misery.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: But first, answer me one question.
He cocks his gun, lining it up between Igor's eyes.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Back when we were chained in the Bone Garden, you saved us.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: What deal did you make with Baba Yaga—the old hag of death—to free us from slavery?

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Or rather, what did you trade for those extraordinary powers that even Arcana was willing to bargain for? Powers that don't belong to a mixed-blood like you.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Just shoot already.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Still clinging to your secrets? Seems you too have lost yourself to the witchcraft of death, my old comrade.
Scorn and arrogance shadow every inch of Krutov's face.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Fine, then take your secrets to the grave.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Farewell.
A flash of sunlight glints in his eyes.
No. That's not sunlight.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: What?
He instinctively looks up toward the light.
A Blazefuse cylinder is hurtling through the air, its active solution burning like a tiny sun.
*bang*
A one-eyed sniper fires, shattering it.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Ugh! Ah. Aahhh!
Scalding alchemical fluid splashes over half of Krutov's face, shrieks of pain mingling with the smell of cooking flesh.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Any morphine to ease the pain, Captain?
Freed from Krutov's incantation, the ground begins to harden again. Ptolemy lowers his gun and pulls his father up before his legs are sealed for good.
They stand side by side.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Thank you, Father.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Just as you predicted, in his anger, he dropped his guard. But I still think I should've aimed for his heart instead!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: An eye for an eye. That was my promise.
He glances past Ptolemy's shoulder at the man he once fought beside.
Krutov kneels, his burned face buried in his hand, the charred skin sticking to his cold leather gloves.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No mortal can transcend eternity, Krutov. I already told you this.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: The power Manus Vindictae offers is nothing but a poisoned chalice. Drinking it down will only lead to your doom.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: No ...

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I'm no weakling like you, Igor! I won't flinch from the pursuit of strength!
His whole body is quivering.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I won't make the same mistake you did!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Wait, what's he holding?
Between his hands and ruined flesh, a familiar dark mask appears.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Forgive my earlier ignorance, Your Holiness. From this moment on, I will eternally praise Your name.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Goddammit!
Ptolemy fires at Krutov, but the bullet hits a wall of ice before it reaches him.
Krutov shakes and murmurs to himself as he undergoes the trial. Ptolemy paces forward, readying himself to tear the mask from him.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: I'll smash that mask to pieces!

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: No, stay back!
Igor grabs his shoulder and pulls him back. A sharp wall of ice slices through the air in front of him.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: I hear it. I hear Your wise words! I should've listened to you long ago. I should've seen the truth of this world! Argh!
Krutov lowers his hands, the melted flesh of his face drooping like soft wax in sticky amber threads.

items.speaker: Krutov
items.text: Heh. Heh. Mother of Resurrection.
With the hand-shaped mask cradling his eyes, a whirlwind of chilling air begins to spread from Krutov.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: This cold, it's ... I see.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Krutov has passed the mask trial. That Manus ritualist must be hiding nearby. She's given him the power to contain the entire stolen winter on his own.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: What? So that's why the Flying Witches couldn't fully stop the ritual. Who'd have thought Krutov was ...
Igor draws his shashka. It trembles in the sudden cold, frost forming in diamonds along its blade.

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: Inform Lieutenant Lilya at once. We've found the final rite.
Living ice swirls and bites at their wrists, climbing up their arms to their torsos. Only their red-hot gun barrels are able to fight it off.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Damn it! This bastard won't hold back the winter any longer!

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Keep shooting!
Manus soldiers, one after another, throw themselves into the gunfire before they reach the collapsed Krutov. Soon, Krutov is submerged in a black tide of soldiers.
Ptolemy swings open his gun cylinder and empties the spent shells.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Damn it! Where'd he run off to?

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: Hey, Flying Witch! How'd those Manus scum appear all of a sudden? Did the cavalry all turn tail and run?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Shut your trap!
A flurry of condensation clouds from her mouth. The thinness of the stinging cold air has pulled her lower.
Lilya runs a circle around the battlefield, knocking aside some straggling enemies, before landing in a small clearing at its center.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The cavalry are chasing down whatever's left of Krutov's bandits. As for the Manus, I got no clue how they managed to disappear like that.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Must've used some kind of teleport ritual. The Alphas are looking for it now.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: There were a lot of them, so the ritual site must be nearby, probably somewhere in the village.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: If that's the case, the Alphas can't do much—too many buildings. You better have your men do a grid search.

items.speaker: Ptolemy
items.text: How about we carpet-bomb them out?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What about the villagers, huh? What about your own men? Is your brain frozen?

items.speaker: Igor
items.text: A unit will be dispatched to perform a ground search, but they won't be as fast as you, Lieutenant.
She has no words. After a moment, she clicks her tongue and climbs onto her broom.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Based on the direction of their reinforcements, the teleport ritual site must be in the south of the village. Brrrr, freezing my butt off here.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Mm! Where is the damn thing? A whole army went through it. No way it'd just disappear without a trace.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Damn it!
Lilya squints as a glare from somewhere on the ground almost blinds her. She banks hard, just barely avoiding a roof.
She tries to hide in the clouds, but the glare follows her every turn.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I swear, if I catch the ground-duster who dares dazzle me right now, I'll give him a missile to the face.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Missile ... to the face ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And Sergey, if you shine the light off that telescope into my eyes one more time ...

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: The last thing you'll see is a missile to the face. Understood?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Ahh. Understood, Lieutenant.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Sergey?!
She pulls down her goggles, drops lower, and searches for the light's source.
It's a pair of binoculars, half shattered, looking like a sorry children's kaleidoscope.
They're in the hands of a wounded young rider in Zeno uniform, looking just as tattered.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Hey! Lieutenant—!
He waves as he jumps, lively as a grassland hare, one hand pointed.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What's he pointing at? Uhm, the stable? Why?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: There something in the stable? Wait! It's got to be Krutov!
She spots a limping Krutov being led into a stable by the ritualist.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: I see them, Sergey! Stay back!
Ice and dust scatter in the explosion.
By the time Lilya lands near the ruined stable, Sergey is already digging through the wreckage like a mole.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Didn't I tell you to stay away? Krutov and that ritualist could still be alive down there.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: No. It can't be. How?
Sergey climbs out, brushes himself off, and runs to the lieutenant.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: The place is tiny, but I don't see them, not even a trace.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Tsk, they got away again.
Lilya kicks a small mushroom at her feet in frustration.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Probably used multiple short-range teleport rituals. Damn! Hopefully the Alphas find something elsewhere.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: So, how did you end up here?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: We can save that for later, Lieutenant. All that matters now is that I'm alive!

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: For a moment, I honestly thought that this would be it for me.
He almost stumbles over his words to get his next question out.

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: How are things in the city? What's happened to Commander Ivan and the rest of the Corps?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: It looks like the bandits and the Manus are gone. What's going on?

items.speaker: Sergey
items.text: Come on, tell me, did we win?
Lilya crosses her arms, not knowing where to begin.
She takes a long drink from a flask she hasn't opened in a long time.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: *sigh*
Winter returns. And with it, the eerie silence of snow.
A distant sound answers for her.
Hollered voices, snorting horses, and the stirring of the long grass all echo on the banks of the shimmering Don.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: They did what they could.
Some sins can never be redeemed. Yet, it is not too late to keep them from spreading, from taking root again.
For one's own sake, and for the sake of home and family.
Bare fists struck steel behemoths; soft flesh warded off fell sorcery.
Their brittle lives were laid down so that others might be spared.
And the living lift their eyes as the first snow falls.
Time finds its rightful course once more. Winter has come.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Luckily, we won, for this round, at least.
